description: Sheet formed individually on a wire mould, carrying a ragged untrimmed deckle edge and usually a high rag-fibre content. Cockerell treats the hand process as a rough guarantee of fibre quality and notes a fashion for leaving such sheets fully untrimmed.
name: hand-made paper

source_ref.label: Douglas Cockerell, Bookbinding and the Care of Books (1902), Chapter XX, p.280. Internet Archive.
